youtube.title: Her Last Words Were a Riddle | Amelia Earhart
youtube.description:
On 2 July 1937, Amelia Earhart and navigator Fred Noonan vanished while flying their Lockheed Electra from Lae, New Guinea, toward tiny Howland Island. Her last known message, at 8:43 a.m.: "We are on the line 157 337." Three theories: they crashed and sank (the official view), they landed on Nikumaroro (where 13 bones, a shoe and a sextant box were found in 1940), or they were captured by Japan. Which do you believe?

📂 Case File #014: Amelia Earhart

Sources: National Geographic, "Top 3 theories for Amelia Earhart's disappearance": https://www.nationalgeographic.com/history/article/amelia-earhart-disappearance-theories-spd
Images: public domain (Earhart portraits; Howland Island, USFWS); Lockheed Electra 12A by Alan Wilson, CC BY-SA 2.0 (similar model); Nikumaroro map CC BY 2.0 (Wikimedia Commons).
Narration voice: AI.
